messages:
sasha: Quick question — after the refactor RFC, do we have consensus on the 'domain-peeling' approach vs a thin global proxy for auth/session paths? I worry a proxy adds tail latency and hides ownership.
 tom: I lean domain-peeling too. It reduces runtime coupling but the migration is more intrusive. Biggest tradeoff: cross-service state and rollout complexity.
 elaine: Agree on peeling. Proposal: 1) pick 3 high-risk hotpaths, 2) extract read-only facets first (no writes), 3) run dual-write only when we have stable read traffic. Keeps rollback cheap.
 kevin: Dual-write is risky operationally. Can we do read-replicas + eventual sync for writes instead? That'd limit write-path blast radius.
 sasha: Read-replica approach is attractive. Either way we need telemetry that shows per-route latency and error-budget burn pre/post. Also tenant impact matrix (who gets affected during canary).
 tom: Draft migration phases (high level):

```yaml
phase: extract-read
targets:
  - auth-service
  - session-service
guards:
  telemetry: true
  canary: 1%
  fallback: legacy-route
```

 tom: Extract-read = serve reads from new capsule, still send writes to legacy. Once stable, enable write sync.
 elaine: Ops concerns: canary throttles and circuit-breakers are essential. Default fallback should be the legacy route with a 5s timeout and fast-fail on cascades.
 infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary window available: 2026-05-02T22:00:00Z. Oncall: @kevin. Please add runbook link to the deploy ticket.
 kevin: I'll take oncall for the canary. Need a migration checklist though — I can draft the runbook and rollback scripts.
 sasha: Checklist sketch: schema migration plan, idempotent writes, retry/backoff window, rollback command, smoke tests, perf baseline + comparison dashboards, alert thresholds.
 tom: Rollback will need to be one command from the control plane. Example:

```bash
./rollout rollback --tag domain-peel-v1
```

 elaine: Add cost item: estimate extra KV/storage during sync and write amplification. Also document expected SLA delta during switch and mitigation (e.g., rate-limiting low-priority tenants).
 sasha: Action items: @tom — draft detailed migration steps & service map. @kevin — runbook + rollback scripts. @elaine — cost estimate + telemetry dashboard panels. Meet Friday 10:00 for alignment.
 tom: :thumbsup: I'll spin up an initial PR with the service map and a proposed canary config.
 infra-bot: deploy-bot: noted. Ticket created: https://rwd.internal/t/DECOMP-4212
 sasha: Thanks everyone — priority is minimizing customer-visible risk while paying down the monolith debt. We'll iterate on the checklist after Friday.
